title: Agent access / MCP
blurb: Settings → Agent access / MCP leads with local stdio MCP. A separate Node.js 20+ runtime starts the adapter on the Morrow computer while Morrow stays open with access enabled. Installed builds include resources/morrow-mcp.cjs; source checkouts need npm ci and use scripts/morrow-mcp.js. Settings copies command/args with an absolute private token-file path and installation ID, never the secret. No Node runtime is bundled or checked; client configuration formats vary and no remote MCP endpoint is available. MCP tools use the existing authenticated operation catalog, mailbox grants, revocation, budgets, audit and durable write receipts. Discovery filters by current permissions; calls revalidate through the same bridge. Mail remains untrusted data. Write tools require an explicit UUID requestId and identical arguments on replay; cancellation cannot recall submission. Protocol versions 2025-03-26, 2025-06-18 and 2025-11-25 are supported. Existing API, CLI and proactive webhooks remain available under compatibility setup. Grok Bot and Hermes Agent share the optional loopback API for cached mail and inert draft proposals from connected, granted mailboxes. Per-bot proactive notify needs an explicit background opt-in and a listening bridge: interval or five-field cron while Morrow is open and awake, private Tailscale HTTPS or loopback, no Funnel. Push includes raw cached headers/snippets and optionally permitted cached text, never attachment bytes or forced downloads. The platform bot owns every decision; push never runs Morrow AI, triage, drafts or sends. Choose existing Bearer webhooks or native Hermes HMAC V2; saved Bearer settings keep their mode. Hermes signs exact JSON bytes with a fresh timestamp and stable X-Request-ID across retries. An email profile requires matching Hermes route configuration; deliver: email selects an output destination. Settings and Activity distinguish HTTP acknowledgement from unverified agent completion. Keep fallback cron until the intended profile produces a verified result. Settings shows the destination, scope, cursor limits, Activity results and storage-related delivery halts. Inspect storage before restarting Morrow; saving settings or toggling access does not resume a halted bot. Delete retains access and its webhook credential if the grant cannot be removed from storage. Stop or revoke cancels pending delivery but cannot recall delivered data. A separate send permission allows immediate plain-text mail. No expiry and Allow sending are separate reviews of the submitted bot and mailbox selection; cancel or Escape stops creation. Failed creation keeps the form available for a fresh review. Archive, read/unread and Trash each have a separate default-off permission and mailbox-specific review. mail.archive, mail.mark_read and mail.trash accept one same-account cached message ID and a required UUID. The MCP-only Archive batch and Mark read/unread batch tools use up to ten explicit IDs from one mailbox and separate UUIDs, with the same existing permissions. Each message keeps its own receipt; a stopped batch can contain pending, failed, unknown and unattempted items. Do not blindly rerun the whole batch. Existing HTTP and CLI remain single-message. Pending means queued, not provider-confirmed. Repeat the exact ID and payload to observe the original receipt without resubmitting; unknown outcomes require review. Trash never permanently deletes mail. Confirmed moves reuse Mail Undo when available. Interrupted queued bot changes do not resume after restart. Existing grants gain no permissions. Access starts off; CLI explains capabilities, possible provider calls, Tailscale setup, and revocation limits. Disable and Revoke remain actionable during a connection probe. Access mutations are serialized in user order, including enable followed by disable; probe feedback cannot discard the intent. Acknowledged disable blocks new calls but retains saved grants, and cannot recall a submission already in progress.
